segments.text: in this video I want to answer the
question what is a requirements
traceability Matrix
and also how do you create one
[Music]
a requirements traceability Matrix is a
grid that links customers users and
other stakeholders service product or
process requirements
to the deliverables that will satisfy
them
requirements traceability matrices are
most often used in software projects
there they connect user requirements to
the different elements of the final
system
they also document the test cases which
will demonstrate that the system meets
the user's requirements
so a requirements traceability Matrix is
a way of tracking each need
through the project process
to make sure that the deliverables can
meet all of the requirements
it's also a valuable tool for assessing
change requests and also for tracking
those change requests once they've been
approved
this means that in many projects
requirements traceability Matrix is a
core document in the scope management
process
in a basic requirements traceability
Matrix each requirement will have a
number of pieces of information attached
to it
primarily it will have a unique ID
number and a description of the
requirements
then there will be some form of
reference to the user the custom or the
stakeholder who requires it maybe it
will be to the function or the division
that is requesting it or maybe it will
be to individual stakeholders
next we need to document the need or the
opportunity that the requirement will
fulfill
and finally of course we need to
identify the deliverables that will meet
the requirement and we usually do this
by reference to work breakdown structure
or product breakdown structure index
however a requirements traceability
Matrix may also include a number of
other pieces of information about each
requirement
it may include any quality or design
specifications that the deliverables
need to meet
so that they can properly address the
requirement
there may be some documentation of
indicative use cases and we may include
information about the development
process the deliverables that will meet
the requirement
we may also include in our requirements
traceability Matrix information for
tracking changes through the project
process
and finally particularly in the it Arena
we would expect a requirements
traceability Matrix to document the test
cases and the scenarios that the
deliverables need to be put through
demonstrate conformance with the
requirements
primarily there are three types of
requirements traceability Matrix
these are forwards traceability
backwards traceability and
bi-directional traceability
forwards traceability Maps each
requirement to the test cases that will
demonstrate it
it establishes definitively that each
requirement has a test case that will
demonstrate it
backwards traceability maps from each
test case to the requirements that
generated
the benefit of this approach is that it
helps to reduce scope creep because if
we introduce an additional requirement
later on it becomes orphaned against the
set of test cases
bi-directional traceability combines
forwards and backwards traceability into
one document
each requirement has test cases and each
test case has requirements
it closes all of the loops
there are a number of requirements
traceability tools and the first to
consider is software tools there are a
number of software tools that embed
requirements traceability matrices
within the tool
going one step further a lot of basic
project management software tools like
Monday Asana jira click up Avro make it
very easy to construct requirements
traceability matrices within the tool
some will almost certainly have user
templates that you can draw upon
but frankly it's also very easy to
construct a simple requirements
traceability Matrix using basic
spreadsheet software
and if you're interested there is a
requirements traceability Matrix within
our templates toolkit
I'll put a link to it in the description
so a requirements traceability Matrix is
a useful scope management tool to
demonstrate that what the users and the
customers and all of your stakeholders
need is actually represented by the
deliverables that you create in your
project
